notes: We investigated growth trends in dry-marginal beech, linden and oak populations on three sites in the natural ecotone from mesic beech forests to more xeric oak forests in Southeastern Europe (western Romania). In a space-for-time approach the region was selected from climate change scenarios (RCP models 2.6, 4.5 and 8.5), identifying it as climate analogue to predicted climates for large parts of Central Europe in 2070. Our results show declining growth trends for beech (Fagus sylvatica) and linden (Tilia tomentosa) due to drought exposure, which is not evident for the investigated oak species (Q. petraea, Q. cerris and Q. frainetto), which recommends the latter for silviculture in a warmer and drier climate in future. This multi-species, multi-site dendroecological data set is novel, highlighting differences in the drought sensitivity of five temperate tree species.
